- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days; model tends to peak too high and then correct.
- Underestimate in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; model fails to capture sharp downward trends or mean reversion.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 79.80 → 80.43) — model overreacts and holds high prices longer than reality.
- Model consistently underestimates low-price periods (e.g., 60–65 range) and overestimates mid-range (70–75) — adjust for volatility clustering.
- Lag in response to recent price drops — model takes 2–3 days to reflect true downward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high for extended periods after peaks, ignoring historical volatility decay.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts show persistent bias toward overestimating early and underestimating late — apply weighted correction with higher weight on first 10 days and last 5 days.
